summary: NorthBridge enterprise: session resumption failures, repeated reconnects and billing token duplication (post-incident)
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 at ~11:05 UTC NorthBridge experienced widespread session resumption failures for long-lived streaming connections to their Dedicated pool in eu-west. Impact: customers saw repeated streaming disconnects, long-tail generation latency, and an unexpected billing spike due to duplicate token accounting for rapid reconnect sequences. Environment: Dedicated pool (eu-west), pinned model redwood/gpt-neox-20b-v1, autoscaler canary rolled out for Dedicated the previous night.

Observed behavior:
- Client sessions were disconnected with TCP FIN or gRPC CANCELs and immediately reconnected in tight loops (seconds).
- Reconnected sessions were frequently routed to new nodes without warm KV caches, causing cold-start generation latency (10s+ for some requests).
- Billing records showed duplicate token counts for reconnects where the same logical session emitted tokens on two nodes within the dedupe window.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Use a long-lived streaming session with continuous prefix context (~4k tokens) against a Dedicated pool using the canary autoscaler.
2) Simulate spikes in prefix-loading by sending a burst of requests with long contexts.
3) Observe node health-check churn and client reconnects.

Relevant logs and artifacts:
- SRE dashboard (Grafana): dashboard/dedicated/session-churn (snapshots attached in Confluence).
- Serving-runtime logs: /var/log/serving-runtime/eu-west/2026-03-12-session-churn.log (error sequences show probe timeouts followed by model cache eviction).
- Billing ledger excerpt: billing/ledgers/northbridge/2026-03-12.csv (duplicate token events flagged).

Initial customer impact: multiple production jobs for NorthBridge failed, reporting up to 40% increased cost for the affected window and degraded SLA latency. Customer escalated via account team at 11:20 UTC.
comments: 2026-03-12 11:22 UTC - Support (Sofia Patel): Acknowledged and opened major incident. Notified SRE and Dedicated infra. Escalated to product. First update due at 11:40 UTC.

2026-03-12 11:35 UTC - SRE (Marco Reyes): Observed elevated health-check failures on dedicated nodes (eu-west). Correlates with autoscaler canary rollout 02:00 UTC. Hypothesis: probe sensitivity + cache warmup causing nodes to be marked unhealthy during prefix load.
2026-03-12 12:05 UTC - Customer (NorthBridge, Amelia Cho): Impacting reporting pipelines. Please advise immediate mitigation; billing spike is causing concern.

2026-03-12 12:20 UTC - Infra (Liam O'Connor): Rolling back autoscaler canary to previous stable release for affected pools. Requesting customer to verify connection stability. Patch in flight to change probe thresholds.
2026-03-12 13:00 UTC - Support (Sofia Patel): Customer confirmed sessions stabilized after rollback. Opening follow-up for billing reconciliation and root cause analysis. Adding to postmortem agenda.

2026-03-13 09:10 UTC - Billing (Rina Gupta): Investigated duplicate token accounting. Implemented temporary dedupe on token events for reconnects within 30s window. Preparing credit estimate for NorthBridge.

2026-03-14 15:40 UTC - Product (Dr. Evan Miller): Final fix merged to adjust health-check logic and autoscaler race conditions. Will schedule a controlled canary next week with synthetic session tests.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 11:05 UTC - first disconnect spikes; 11:18 UTC - repeated reconnects and billing counters increase; 11:30 UTC - canary identified as common factor; 12:20 UTC - rollback executed; 12:50 UTC - customer reports stabilization.

Root cause (summary): A regression in the new autoscaler/health-probe logic introduced last deployment caused nodes to be marked unhealthy while model KV caches were loading under load. This produced rapid node churn, which caused clients to reconnect repeatedly and sometimes produce duplicate token accounting when token events were emitted from two different nodes for the same logical client window.

Contributing factors: 1) Health-check thresholds did not account for short-lived GPU memory spikes during cache warmup. 2) Autoscaler race: node termination and replacement overlapped with client reconnect logic. 3) Billing pipeline lacked robust de-duplication for near-simultaneous token events tied to a session ID.

Evidence: serving-runtime traces show probe failures preceding gRPC CANCELs. Node metrics show GPU memory usage spikes at model load events. Billing ledger shows identical session IDs generating token events on distinct node IDs within <5s.

Temporary mitigations taken: autoscaler canary rollback, deployed billing dedupe rule (30s window), added short-lived session-affinity toggle for Dedicated pools, alerted customer and applied pro-rated credit hold while we complete postmortem.

Permanent fixes planned: patch health-check to use GPU-memory-aware thresholds and 'cache warming' grace period; fix autoscaler lifecycle race to ensure in-flight connections are drained before node termination; enhance billing ingestion to dedupe token events by session_id + token_hash within 60s; add synthetic long-lived streaming tests in canary pipeline.
Cross-references: infra PR 3145 reverts the canary changes; serving-runtime PR 2201 adds cache-warmup awareness to health probes; Confluence postmortem draft created for 2026-03-12.
Customer communication: account team sent incident timeline and commit to credits and follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-15.

Open follow-ups assigned: postmortem owner: Evan Miller; QA owner: Priya Singh; Billing reconciliation owner: Rina Gupta; Timeline for fixes: target 2026-03-22 for full deploy to prod after canary verification.
resolution_notes: Workaround/fix: Immediate rollback of the autoscaler canary restored session stability. Billing dedupe rule applied to stop further duplicate charges and a pro-rated credit was applied to NorthBridge for the affected window. Permanent fixes deployed to the canary branch: (1) health-check adjusted to tolerate short GPU cache warmups, (2) autoscaler lifecycle fixed to drain connections before termination, (3) billing dedupe logic enhanced. Rollout notes: changes merged to main on 2026-03-13; controlled canary scheduled for 2026-03-18 with synthetic streaming loadtests. Follow-ups: complete postmortem write-up, add automated synthetic test to canary pipeline, run a joint validation session with NorthBridge before re-enabling autoscaler canary on their pools. Customer compensation: pro-rated credit estimated at $6,400 for the incident window; invoice adjustment in progress.
